title: Regular and irregular verbs
metaTitle: Irregular Spanish verbs list: present, indefinido and participle – Reference – icanspeak Spanish
description: Regular, irregular and stem-changing Spanish verbs at a glance: the yo form of the present, the él form of the indefinido and the participle, grouped by pattern.
lead: Three forms tell you most of what you need about a Spanish verb: yo in the present, él in the indefinido, and the participle. Verbs that change in the same way are grouped together.

sections.name: Regular verbs
sections.what: Take the ending off the infinitive (-ar, -er, -ir) and add the regular endings. Most verbs work like this, and new verbs do too: tuitear, tuiteó, tuiteado.
regel: Pattern: *hablar: hablo · habló · hablado.* *comer: como · comió · comido.* *vivir: vivo · vivió · vivido.*
The accent changes the word: *hablo* = I speak, *habló* = he or she spoke.
-er and -ir verbs share their indefinido endings and their participle: *comió, vivió; comido, vivido.*
Spelling keeps the sound in the yo form of the indefinido: *buscar → busqué, llegar → llegué, empezar → empecé.* The él form stays regular: *buscó, llegó, empezó.*
A vowel before the ending turns -ió into -yó: *leer → leyó, creer → creyó, construir → construyó.*
items: In much of Latin America also: rentar.
# Regular, with a spelling change in yo of the indefinido
# Regular, with y in the indefinido
y in the present too: construyes, construye.

sections.name: Irregular verbs
sections.what: These change in one or more of the three forms. The most common verbs in Spanish are here, so learn them first.
regel: Many irregular verbs take a new stem in the indefinido and lose the accent: *tener → tuvo, hacer → hizo, poner → puso, decir → dijo.*
*ser* and *ir* have the same indefinido: *fue, fueron.* The sentence tells you which one it is: *Fue médico.* (ser) / *Fue a Madrid.* (ir)
The yo form can be the only irregular form in the present: *salir → salgo*, but *sales, sale.*
After *haber*, the participle never changes: *he hecho, ha escrito, hemos visto.*
items: In much of Latin America, caminar is more usual for “to walk”.
# New stem with j: ellos -eron, not -ieron
ellos condujeron. In most of Latin America: manejar.
# New stem and an irregular participle
z only in él/ella: yo hice, él hizo.
# Irregular yo in the present only
oyes, oye, oyen in the present.

sections.name: Stem-changing verbs
sections.what: The last vowel of the stem changes in the present when it is stressed: quiero, but queremos. The indefinido and the participle are usually regular.
regel: Pattern: *e → ie, o → ue, e → i, u → ue.* The vowel changes in all the present forms except *nosotros* and *vosotros*: *duermo, duermes, duerme, dormimos, dormís, duermen.*
-ar and -er verbs keep the regular vowel in the indefinido: *pensó, volvió.*
-ir verbs change the vowel in él and ellos of the indefinido: *pedir → pidió, pidieron; dormir → durmió, durmieron; preferir → prefirió, prefirieron.*
A stem-changing verb can have an irregular participle too: *volver → vuelto, morir → muerto, resolver → resuelto.*
items: Mostly in él/ella and ellos: cuesta, cuestan.
g → j before o: elijo, but eliges.
